B-6 For each point P in $B ,$ let $S _ { P }$ be the set of points with all coordinates equal $\mathrm { t o } \pm 1$ which differ from P in exactly one coordinate. Since there are more than $2 ^ { n + 1 } / n$ points in $B ,$ and each $S _ { P }$ has n elements, the cardinalities of the sets $S _ { P }$ add up to more than $2 ^ { n + 1 }$ , which is to say, more than twice the total number of points. By the pigeonhole principle, there must be a point in three of the sets, say $S _ { P } , S _ { Q } , S _ { R }$ . But then any two of $P , Q , R$ differ in exactly two coordinates, so $P Q R$ is an equilateral triangle, as desired.
